external_entities.name: Customer
external_entities.description: A customer who browses and places orders through the mobile app and receives a faxed confirmation.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: Mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application customers use to browse and order socks.

processes.name: Web API
processes.description: The API used by the mobile app that keeps customer information and hands orders to SIMS.
processes.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database
processes.notes: Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication.

processes.name: SIMS
processes.description: The stock and inventory system that receives orders, writes delivery addresses, and sends dispatch notes.

processes.name: Fax gateway
processes.description: The gateway that dials the number stored against an order and faxes a confirmation to the customer.
processes.source_excerpt: the fax gateway, which faxes the customer a confirmation
processes.notes: Nobody checks it arrived at the right place.

processes.name: Macros
processes.description: Spreadsheet macros that send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy.
processes.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API
processes.notes: It was a stopgap and it is still here.

data_stores.name: User database
data_stores.description: The database holding customer name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the user database is encrypted.

data_stores.name: Flat file
data_stores.description: A flat file kept alongside SIMS containing only delivery addresses.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a flat file kept alongside it — only addresses go in that file, nothing else
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the flat file is encrypted.

data_stores.name: Spreadsheet
data_stores.description: The catalogue spreadsheet kept on a marketing laptop in the office.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet

data_flows.name: browse and order
data_flows.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

data_flows.name: HTTP requests
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP — not HTTPS
data_flows.notes: Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication.

data_flows.name: store customer data
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database
data_flows.data_description: Customer name, address, and the card they paid with

data_flows.name: hand order
data_flows.source_excerpt: the API hands the order over to SIMS

data_flows.name: write address
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file

data_flows.name: send dispatch note
data_flows.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway

data_flows.name: fax confirmation
data_flows.source_excerpt: which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it
data_flows.notes: Nobody checks it arrived at the right place.
data_flows.data_description: Confirmation with the customer's name and address

data_flows.name: change prices
data_flows.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

trust_boundaries.name: Customer device
trust_boundaries.description: The customer-controlled environment hosting the mobile app.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

trust_boundaries.name: Office
trust_boundaries.description: The office environment where the marketing laptop and spreadsheet are located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

assumptions.assumption: The customer mobile app runs in a customer-controlled device environment.
assumptions.basis: The text places the mobile app with customers, implying a zone controlled by a different party.

assumptions.assumption: The mobile app is in the customer device environment.
assumptions.basis: The app is described as a mobile app used by customers.

assumptions.assumption: The customer is in the customer device environment.
assumptions.basis: The customer uses the mobile app from the customer-side environment.

assumptions.assumption: The office is a network boundary.
assumptions.basis: The text places the marketing laptop and spreadsheet in the office, implying a distinct office network location.

assumptions.assumption: The spreadsheet is in the office boundary.
assumptions.basis: The text says the spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

assumptions.assumption: The macros are in the office boundary.
assumptions.basis: The macros run in the spreadsheet located on the marketing laptop in the office.
It contains customer names, addresses, and payment card information.
